newsitem.title: UK: Japan funds selling local equities -- Merrill poll.
newsitem.headline: Japan funds selling local equities -- Merrill poll.

text.p: Japanese fund managers have become net sellers of their own equity market for the first time since summer 1995 on the view that economic activity in 1997 will be subdued, a Merrill Lynch survey shows.

The poll of 43 institutions responsible for funds totalling $546 billion was conducted December 2-3 and indicated sellers outnumber buyers by two percent. In October, buyers outnumbered sellers by 15 percent.
The number of economic bulls is down to 60 percent from 67 percent in November and 96 percent in January 1996.
Earnings per share forecasts are being downgraded, falling to 8.1 percent in 1996 from the 8.9 percent estimated last month. The forecast for 1997 is now 6.8 percent from 7.4 percent in November.
Some 77 percent believe land prices in Japan have further to fall.
The poll showed that fund managers were still keen on Europe and Asian equities and that the trend is away from reducing cash. They are selling Japanese bonds and buying US bonds.
On the Japanese economy, some 58 percent expect the key discount rate to be higher in a year's time.
The dollar is the favoured currency, followed by the yen, mark and sterling.
